create_rusty_copper.configuration.title: %s Configuration
create_rusty_copper.configuration.rustPe: Configure extra stress consumption from copper oxidation. Waxing and casing preserve the current penalty. Create's disableStress setting also disables these penalties.
create_rusty_copper.configuration.enable: Enable additional stress consumption for exposed, weathered, and oxidized copper components.
create_rusty_copper.configuration.expose: Additional stress per component per RPM. Zero disables the exposed-stage penalty.
create_rusty_copper.configuration.weathe: Additional stress per component per RPM. Zero disables the weathered-stage penalty.
create_rusty_copper.configuration.oxidiz: The very high default overloads ordinary networks and stops all connected machinery. This is a finite stress cost; enough capacity can overcome it. Zero disables the oxidized-stage penalty.
Copper Shafts relay rotation in a straight line.
create_rusty_copper.ponder.copper_shaft_: Brass or Andesite Casing can be used to decorate Copper Shafts.
Unwaxed Copper Shafts oxidize over time through four stages.
By default, each later oxidation stage consumes more stress capacity.
Fully oxidized shafts can overstress the whole connected network and stop it.
The result depends on the server's rust penalty settings and the network's stress capacity.
Casing does not prevent oxidation or remove its stress cost.
Right-click with an Axe to scrape off one oxidation stage at a time.
Honeycomb waxes copper at its current stage and prevents further oxidation.
Wax preserves existing oxidation and its stress cost.
On waxed copper, the first Axe use removes only the wax.
Use the Axe again to remove the next oxidation stage.
Scrape first, then wax to protect clean copper without a rust penalty.
